skill.name: generating-storyboards
skill.description: Generates the storyboard sheets for a video — one image per clip, panels in a row, each panel one action. Divides each clip into panels itself, then builds the sheets one at a time, each taking the previous one as a reference, so the person and product stay consistent except where the story deliberately changes them. Use when a video's clip lengths and story are settled and it needs sheets before anything is animated. Not for a still image on its own — that should be made using generating-images.
skill.summary: Creates consistent storyboard sheets for each video clip using visual references and structured panel planning.
skill.author: supercmohq

content.value_statement: Video concepts often lack precise shot continuity before production begins. This skill converts settled clip plans into reference-driven storyboard sheets with structured panels.
actual_capabilities: Divides each planned clip into panels based on actions and duration.
Writes camera position, framing, action, hand placement, product details, and performance for every panel.
Uses person, product, and previous-sheet images as ordered visual references.
Builds one 16:9 storyboard sheet per clip with vertical panels.
Carries setting, wardrobe, product state, and subject appearance across consecutive sheets.
Polls pending image-generation jobs without starting duplicate billed requests.
limitations: Requires a settled video story, clip durations, and reference images before generation.
Creates static storyboard sheets, not finished videos or standalone promotional images.
Generates sheets sequentially because each later sheet depends on the previous result.
Image models may still produce inaccurate hands, faces, labels, or product geometry.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Advertisement
use_cases.description: Turn approved product beats and timing into sequential storyboard sheets before video generation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Client Review
use_cases.description: Present camera choices, actions, and visual continuity for approval before committing production resources.

use_cases.title: Map Social Video Clips
use_cases.description: Convert a short-form script into practical panels with varied framing and realistic product handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a storyboard for [clip description]. The clip lasts [seconds]. Use the supplied person and product references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when one clip and its required references are ready.

prompt_templates.title: Storyboard a Short Advertisement
prompt_templates.prompt: Build storyboard sheets for this [duration] advertisement. Follow these clip beats: [beats]. Keep [person], [product], wardrobe, and setting consistent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a complete advertisement plan already defines clip timing.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Storyboard each planned clip using [visual look]. Preserve the reference lighting and product scale. Vary camera position, framing, and expression across panels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when art direction and visual references are approved.

prompt_templates.title: Enforce Complex Continuity
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate sequential storyboard sheets from [clip plan]. Track every object and product state across cuts. Flag any action that exceeds the available duration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for multi-clip concepts with product transformations or detailed continuity.

output_examples.input: Storyboard a six-second skincare clip showing a person lifting and presenting a jar.
output_examples.output: A 16:9 sheet with two vertical panels. Panel one shows the lift; panel two presents the jar with a changed camera angle.

output_examples.input: Create three storyboard sheets for an unboxing sequence using person and package references.
output: Sheet one establishes the sealed package and opening action.
Sheet two continues with the contents removed and the packaging absent.
Sheet three presents the product while preserving appearance, wardrobe, setting, and product scale.

output_examples.input: Storyboard a four-second product detail clip with a rigid bottle.
output_examples.output: A compact sheet with realistic grip mechanics, true product size, one visible product face, and varied close framing.

best_practices: Provide final clip durations, story beats, and visual references before requesting sheets.
State deliberate changes between clips so all other visual details remain consistent.
Review each completed sheet before generating the next dependent sheet.
anti_patterns: Do not request a finished video when the required deliverable is a storyboard.
Do not combine multiple physical actions into one panel.
Do not omit product measurements when realistic scale matters.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces one static 16:9 storyboard sheet per video clip, with vertical panels arranged from left to right.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide clip stories, durations, sheet order, visual direction, and relevant person or product images.

faq.question: Can it create a finished video?
faq.answer: No. It prepares storyboard images for review or later video production.

faq.question: Why are sheets generated sequentially?
faq.answer: Each new sheet uses the preceding sheet as a visual reference for continuity.

faq.question: How many actions belong in one panel?
faq.answer: Each panel should contain one primary continuous action involving one object.

faq.question: Can it preserve product appearance?
faq.answer: It uses product references, fixed naming, measurements, and visible-side constraints, but image-generation errors can still occur.
